study_identification_part.si4_title: Rightward brain structural asymmetry in young children with autism

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Using developmental normative models on sMRI, characterize atypical gray matter volume (GMV) asymmetry in young children with ASD with/without DD/ID and DD/ID-only, and test associations with behavioral/clinical measures and gene expression profiles.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Associations tested between GMV asymmetry deviations and clinical/behavioral measures (ASD symptoms; IQ) via multivariate analyses (e.g., CCA), and spatial associations with gene expression profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD children show rightward GMV asymmetry in inferior parietal and precentral regions; ASD+DD/ID exhibits broader mean deviations; ASD-only shows elevated heterogeneity; DD/ID-only shows no significant asymmetry abnormalities.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: One-sample tests revealed more rightward asymmetry (negative deviations) in inferior parietal and precentral gyri for both ASD groups; ASD+DD/ID also had rightward fusiform/entorhinal and leftward deviations in cingulate/bSTS/paracentral/rostral ACC; ASD-only showed leftward rostral middle frontal. Kurtosis analyses indicated pronounced individual variability in ASD-only across several regions (e.g., entorhinal, fusiform, temporal pole). No significant abnormalities in DD/ID-only. Group patterns overlapped across networks (default mode, ventral attention, somatomotor, visual). Multivariate associations linked deviations with ASD symptoms (ASD-only) and with ASD symptoms plus verbal IQ (ASD+DD/ID).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Demonstrates feasibility of normative modeling of asymmetry in early childhood; potential utility for stratification by deviation profiles and linking to behavioral and genetic measures.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design; potential sedation differences across groups; reliance on ComBat for harmonization (covariate details unspecified); within-cohort validation only (no external dataset).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Two MRI sites/scanners (Philips Ingenia; Siemens Verio); T1-weighted protocols detailed. QC included dual manual reviews and algorithmic checks. Site effects harmonized with ComBat before ROI-wise GPR normative modeling in PCNtoolkit using age and sex covariates. Fivefold CV validated normative fits; high correlations between original and CV deviations (Fig. S3).
